Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Digital payments generate revenue through transaction fees and government revenue collection via RUPE. EMIS charges interbank fees for Multicaixa network operations. The RUPE system has generated significant state revenues — RUPE payments account for 36% of state current revenues according to EMIS. EMIS's 2025 annual results show the network 'moved more than 69 billion kwanzas.' AGT's e-invoicing and SAF-T framework generates fiscal revenue by reducing tax evasion. Consumer-facing services also charge fees on mobile money, transfers, and ATM transactions.

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: Angola has an operational tax portal — the AGT Taxpayer Portal (portaldocontribuinte.minfin.gov.ao) — integrated with EMIS's RUPE payment reference system for electronic tax payments. AGT issued mandatory e-invoicing effective January 1, 2026 for large taxpayers, with digital invoice submission via AGT portal or REST API. SAF-T accounting filings have been mandatory since 2019. The portal allows tax declarations, payments, registration, and invoice management. RUPE enables omni-channel tax payments (bank counters, ATMs, online, mobile).

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: B2B (business-to-business) payments are supported through the EMIS interbank system, credit transfers (STC), RUPE system for B2G/B2B invoice settlement, and the e-invoicing mandate (Decree 71/25) which mandates electronic invoicing for all B2B, B2C and B2G transactions. EMIS's Host-to-Host (H2H) channel supports institutional transactions. Angola's SAF-T regime (since 2019) and mandatory e-invoicing from 2025/2026 further integrate B2B digital payments.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border digital payments are under active development. Angola is a SADC member and the Angolan Kwanza is in the process of being onboarded to SADC-TCIB (Transactions Cleared on Immediate Basis). BNA confirmed that Angola's participation in the SADC-RTGS system will enable Angolan PSPs to join TCIB via the KWiK arrangement for instant cross-border transfers. A cooperation protocol between BNA and Bank of Namibia is underway. Angola's BNA National Payment System Vision 2023-2028 includes cross-border payments via SADC and continental integration. Angola is not yet confirmed as a live PAPSS participant (PAPSS has 15 central banks as of early 2025, Angola not listed among live commercial bank countries). SADC TCIB onboarding of Angolan Kwanza was still 'underway' as of 2024.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: G2P (government-to-person) payments are in active use. The Kwenda cash transfer program (launched May 2020, World Bank-supported, $320M) digitizes social assistance payments to over 1.6 million vulnerable households using mobile money, simplified bank accounts, and ATM cards. As of January 2022, over 502,000 families registered and 247,000 received payments. Government also pays civil service salaries through the banking system. EMIS RUPE system is used for government revenue collection. KWiK roadmap includes payments to the state functionality. G2P digitization is active and growing.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: P2B (person-to-business) payments are supported through multiple channels. Multicaixa POS terminals allow card payments at merchants. QR code payments exceeded 7 million transactions in Angola by November 2025. Afrimoney supports merchant payments. PayPay has 3,000 commercial establishments registered. AGT's e-invoicing mandate (mandatory from Jan 2026 for large taxpayers) further formalises P2B digital payments. KWiK's roadmap includes QR code payments and merchant management.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: P2G (person-to-government) digital payments are actively used. The RUPE (Referência Única de Pagamentos ao Estado) system, operated by EMIS on behalf of the state, enables electronic tax and government fee payments via ATMs, online banking, POS, and mobile channels. The EMIS website states 'RUPE payments already account for 36% of the state's current revenues.' AGT (tax administration) integrated the electronic payments network via RUPE, reducing bank intermediation costs by over 90%. Mandatory e-invoicing from January 2026 with AGT portal integration reinforces P2G digital payments.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: P2P (person-to-person) transfers are fully supported and are a core use case. Multicaixa Express, KWiK, Afrimoney, Unitel Money and other platforms all support P2P transfers. KWiK processed 35 million transactions in 2025 with over 100% growth, primarily P2P. MCX Express has 2+ million active monthly users performing 40+ operations/month. P2P is universal across all Angolan payment platforms.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: The Banco Nacional de Angola (BNA) plays a regulatory and oversight role in the payment system. BNA's Payment Systems Department oversees all payment infrastructure, issues regulations (Instruções/Avisos), and sets policy under Angola's Payment System Law (Law 05/05). BNA co-created KWiK with EMIS and mandates all 22 banks and mobile operators to join the platform. BNA does not directly operate retail systems; EMIS operates the infrastructure. BNA's role is primarily regulatory/oversight with strong policy direction rather than direct operation. Under the World Bank DPF, BNA restructured its payment systems unit for independent oversight.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Angola's Law 23/11 (Electronic Communications and Information Services) mandates that operators immediately notify the APD (Data Protection Agency) and INACOM in the event of a security breach that compromises the integrity of personal data. This constitutes mandatory breach notification. Law 7/17 also requires operators to implement preventive security measures and incident management plans. The obligation is statutory, not discretionary.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Angola has a general data protection law — Law No. 22/11 of 17 June 2011 (Lei de Proteção de Dados Pessoais). This is an omnibus personal data protection law that establishes the National Data Protection Authority (APD), data processing principles, data subject rights, and penalties. Additional related laws include Law 23/11 (Electronic Communications), Law 7/17 (Network and IT Systems Protection), and Criminal Code provisions. The law is general-purpose and not payment-specific, thus classified as general data protection legislation rather than specific payment data provisions.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Angola has partial pro-poor governance in payment systems. The BNA and EMIS launched the 'Cidadão Digital' project which reached 1 million Angolans with digital financial literacy. The Kwenda G2P cash transfer program (World Bank-supported) explicitly targets poor and vulnerable households, integrating digital payments with simplified accounts. Angola's 2025–2027 National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) addresses access gaps. KWiK was specifically designed for financial inclusion of the unbanked. However, ~50% of population remains unbanked, mobile money penetration is only ~6%, and rural infrastructure gaps persist.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No evidence that EMIS or BNA publish detailed scheme rules for the Multicaixa or KWiK payment schemes in a fully public manner. The SADC-CCBG report notes that BNA has oversight policy documents and internal audit manuals, but scheme rules for EMIS-operated networks (e.g. Multicaixa Rules and Procedures Manual - MRP) are referenced as internal governance documents rather than publicly accessible policy. BNA publishes regulatory notices (Instruções/Avisos) on its website, which are public, but detailed operational scheme rules are confidential/internal.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Angola has a well-deployed digital payment system via EMIS (Empresa Interbancária de Serviços), operating the MULTICAIXA ATM/POS network, five national clearing systems, Multicaixa Express mobile app, and the KWiK (Kwanza Instantâneo) instant payment system launched in July 2023. In 2025, EMIS processed billions of transactions and record financial volumes. Coverage remains partial nationwide with urban concentration; rural areas face infrastructure gaps. KWiK serves 23+ million users (2025) but geographic reach is still expanding; mobile money penetration is ~6% nationally.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Overall digital payment active user rate is below 20% of the adult population. Only 31% of Angolans have bank accounts (2025 AFI data). Mobile money penetration is approximately 6% (IDG/USAID 2025 report). KWiK serves 23+ million users of a ~35 million population, but many are registered rather than active. Multicaixa Express has 2.6 million registered / 2 million active monthly users — against a ~20 million adult population, this represents roughly 10% of adults. The GSMA rates Angola's mobile money prevalence as 'very low.' Financial inclusion gap: ~50% unbanked. World Bank Findex data for Angola is not available (N/A in G20 portal), but all indicators point to sub-20% active digital payment usage.

Definition: Whether independent external audits of payment system security, operations, financial controls, and compliance are conducted by third-party auditors, and whether audit results or summaries are made public.
Comments: Private audits of Angola's payment system infrastructure are confirmed. The SPA Law (Law 05/05) mandates yearly external audits of payment system operators (the audit is the responsibility of the operator). EMIS, as operator of MULTICAIXA, is subject to mandatory annual external audits. EMIS achieved Tier III data centre certification from Uptime Institute (a form of technical audit). EMIS has PCI DSS certification for the Multicaixa network. The BNA conducted an audit of retail payment systems (SCV and MULTICAIXA) through an internationally tendered company. BNA also has mandatory half-yearly internal audits of the SPTR (RTGS). No evidence that full audit reports are published publicly; results referenced in internal and BNA oversight reports.

Definition: Whether digital payment systems and access points (apps, USSD, agents) are designed to accommodate persons with disabilities (visual, hearing, mobility, cognitive impairments), and disability-disaggregated coverage rates if data available.
Comments: Partial disability access exists. The Kwenda G2P program includes specific provisions: 'For the elderly and disabled, community workers will go to their homes and provide the benefits in person.' USSD-based payment channels (accessible via basic phones without smartphones) are supported by KWiK for populations who cannot use apps. However, no specific evidence of standardised accessibility features (screen readers, Braille, etc.) built into EMIS or Multicaixa platforms. The primary channels (Multicaixa Express app, ATMs) have limited documented accessibility features. Some agent-assisted channels reduce barriers for people with disabilities.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Government adoption of digital payments is partial (20–49%). Civil servant salaries are paid via the banking system (a BNA initiative to bancarize public sector employees has been ongoing since at least 2010). G2P Kwenda program provides digital social transfers to ~1.6 million targeted families. The RUPE system handles 36% of state current revenues digitally. E-invoicing is mandated for state suppliers from January 2026. However, many government transfers and procurement payments still involve traditional banking or cash channels. The AGT portal is operational but e-invoicing for government suppliers only became mandatory in 2026.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: Partial refugee and migrant access to digital payments. Angola hosts refugees (primarily DRC and other nationalities). The Kwenda program uses a program-specific Kwenda ID card to allow beneficiaries without national IDs to open bank or mobile accounts, partially addressing documentation barriers that affect refugees and migrants. The SADC TCIB initiative aims to improve cross-border payment access for SADC nationals living outside their home countries. However, formal KYC requirements, national ID requirements, and limited agent networks in refugee-hosting areas create barriers. No specific national policy or programme for refugee/migrant financial inclusion through the digital payment system is confirmed.
